Supercharge your developers and AI agents.

Big tasks go better in small steps. Give each step a fresh harness that holds only what that step needs: nothing drifts, and smaller models can do more of the work.

Request an invitation

Search is free
Works with Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
Invitation only while we open in small groups

Harness and agent optimized operation, in plain words: a harness is the program that runs your coding agent, such as Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode. Today your agent can search Baltor's reviewed library at each step and download only what that step needs, with its source, licence and exact version. The fresh harness for each step is being built.

Free to install. Paid access to the library, one plan at 29 United States dollars each month. Your model keys stay with you, and Baltor never asks you for a provider key.

WHY TEAMS USE BALTOR

Right-sized help for every step of the work.

Long sessions drift and large models are costly. Baltor gives each step the material it asks for, so the work stays focused and smaller models can do more of it.

Only the context a step needs

Search returns short references. Your agent downloads only the item it chose, so a small step never carries the whole history.

Available now

Smaller models for smaller decisions

With the right material in front of it, a smaller or local model can take on work that would otherwise need a large one.

Being built

Expertise your agent does not have

A reviewed library of skills. Every item is approved by reviewers who did not write it.

Available now

Reuse code instead of rewriting it

Every item carries its source, licence and exact version, so proven work can be reused rather than generated again.

Code packages coming

Fewer repeated mistakes

What went wrong in earlier work is kept, so the next step can start from it instead of repeating it.

Planned

Long jobs that finish overnight

Work is split into small steps, each in its own fresh harness, so a small model can carry a long task to the end while you are away.

GET STARTED

Three steps to your first download.

Ask for an account, connect the harness you already use, and let your agent ask for what each step needs.

1
Get access
An invitation takes a minute
2
Connect your harness
One entry, no key in files
3
Search and download
Search is free
1. Get access
Request an invitation
Open for requests
Work email
What will your agents work on? Optional

The note helps the person reading your request. Do not include credentials, customer data or anything private.

Request an invitation

A person reads every request and decides. We keep your address and note only to send your invitation, as the privacy notice says, and an operator can erase both from the list on request. We do not publish a date, and we will not add you to a mailing list.

Already invited? Sign in

What an invited account gets
Free access while we open in small groups
The reviewed library, searchable from your harness
A usage record for every download
2. Connect your harness

Your harness connects to this service with the Model Context Protocol. Pick it below and copy one reviewed entry. It holds this service's address and the name of the environment variable with your key, never the key.

Codex
OpenCode 1.x
Claude Code

Your existing Codex config.toml Merge this table into your existing config.toml. Do not replace your other settings.

[mcp_servers.baltor]
url = "https://baltor.ai/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN"
startup_timeout_sec = 20
tool_timeout_sec = 45
Copy configuration without secrets

Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli

Documented configuration; native end-to-end qualification is pending. Check your installed version with codex --version.

Set BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN in your environment. The file holds the variable's name, never the key, so it is safe to keep in version control. Then check the entry with codex mcp list

This command shows configuration, not a completed handshake. In a Codex session, inspect /mcp and confirm that Baltor's tools are available before asking it to search.

Temporary setup in Bash
Check the service connection
Endpoint
https://baltor.ai/mcp
Transport
Streamable HTTP
Protocol
2025-11-25, 2026-07-28
Authentication
Service token, sent in the Authorization header

This browser check initializes the protocol and lists the available operations with your current connection. It does not run any work, fetch file bodies or spend model credits.

Test service connection
Sign in to check access

Sign in with your service token to run the connection check.

Not tested. No model calls are made by this check.

Configuration, connection, retrieval, native loading and useful task completion are separate checks. A green connection does not qualify all five. This service does not offer a browser-based authorization flow for native clients yet. Read the access and data boundaries.

When you no longer need it

If you created this token on your Account page, open Account, find it under Your client tokens and select Revoke. If your operator gave you the token, ask your operator to revoke it. The service refuses a revoked token on its next request. Revoking a token does not recall files that were already downloaded.

After the token is revoked, delete the mcp_servers.baltor table from config.toml and clear BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN from your environment.

Open your account
3. Search and download

Ask your agent to search Baltor for what the current step needs. It gets short references with source, licence and digest, downloads only the one it chooses, and every download appears in your usage.

Open the first example
Search in the browser

Connecting needs nothing installed beside your harness. The engine that runs on your machine is free and open source under the MIT licence; the documentation has its installation steps.

PRICING

One plan.
Search is free.

Baltor Pro is for one person and the devices that person connects. You bring your own tools and your own model keys.

ONE PLAN

Baltor Pro
Invitation only

29 United States dollars
each month

Search is free.
Searching permitted material and reading a reference costs nothing, with an account or with a key from your operator.
The measured unit is one downloaded item.
One item at the version you selected counts once. A search, a second look at the same reference and a refused download are not downloads.
Invited accounts are free.
While invitations go out in small groups, an invited account pays nothing and keeps the same limits as a paid account. An invitation may also carry a discount code.
Personal keys for each device.
Create and revoke a key for every client you connect, from your account page.
Connection settings for OpenCode, Codex and Claude Code.
Copy one reviewed entry. It never holds your key.
Request an invitation
↗
See how it works

Accounts open by invitation. Invited accounts stay free. A signed-in account can subscribe from its account page when checkout is available.

What the price does not cover

Your model provider bills you directly for the calls your own tools make. Baltor does not resell model access and never asks for a model key.

How usage is counted

Your account page shows the usage the service recorded for your connections. That record is the same one the price is based on, so you can check it yourself.

How to stop paying

When payment is open you can cancel from your account page. Cancelling stops the next payment. Files you already downloaded stay on your computer.

What is still in progress

Public account creation and complete native client onboarding are not finished. No percentage saving, replacement of specialist teams or guaranteed daily performance gain is claimed for this service.

2. Connect your harness

Your harness connects to this service with the Model Context Protocol. Pick it below and copy one reviewed entry. It holds this service's address and the name of the environment variable with your key, never the key.

Codex
OpenCode 1.x
Claude Code

Your existing Codex config.toml Merge this table into your existing config.toml. Do not replace your other settings.

[mcp_servers.baltor]
url = "https://baltor.ai/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN"
startup_timeout_sec = 20
tool_timeout_sec = 45
Copy configuration without secrets

Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli

Documented configuration; native end-to-end qualification is pending. Check your installed version with codex --version.

Set BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN in your environment. The file holds the variable's name, never the key, so it is safe to keep in version control. Then check the entry with codex mcp list

This command shows configuration, not a completed handshake. In a Codex session, inspect /mcp and confirm that Baltor's tools are available before asking it to search.

Authentication
Service token, sent in the Authorization header

This browser check initializes the protocol and lists the available operations with your current connection. It does not run any work, fetch file bodies or spend model credits.

Test service connection
Sign in to check access

Sign in with your service token to run the connection check.

Not tested. No model calls are made by this check.

Configuration, connection, retrieval, native loading and useful task completion are separate checks. A green connection does not qualify all five. This service does not offer a browser-based authorization flow for native clients yet. Read the access and data boundaries.

When you no longer need it

If you created this token on your Account page, open Account, find it under Your client tokens and select Revoke. If your operator gave you the token, ask your operator to revoke it. The service refuses a revoked token on its next request. Revoking a token does not recall files that were already downloaded.

After the token is revoked, delete the mcp_servers.baltor table from config.toml and clear BALTOR_SERVICE_TOKEN from your environment.

Open your account
3. Search and download

Ask your agent to search Baltor for what the current step needs. It gets short references with source, licence and digest, downloads only the one it chooses, and every download appears in your usage.

Open the first example
Search in the browser

Connecting needs nothing installed beside your harness. The engine that runs on your machine is free and open source under the MIT licence; the documentation has its installation steps.

SETUP GUIDE

Connect a client.
Keep your keys private.

There are two different connections: access to an intelligence service, and permission for your harness to call a model provider.

Request an invitation
First retrieval example
Access and data boundaries
Technical runtime reference

The public website calls a unit of work a step. The implementation uses the canonical Loop runtime described here and in the repository.

Runtime classification and role profiles
Complete behavior of a discrete cognitive or act step Loop node

Harness Intelligence is a provisioning view over the four persistent layers. It is not a fifth persistent layer.

Runtime Memory is the temporary note board for one run. Saving a note does not promote it into reusable intelligence.

1. Install the local runtime

Use the release and installation instructions supplied by your service operator. When installing this repository from an approved checkout, the serving dependencies are optional:

python -m pip install '.[serving]'
loop-engine service --help

The intelligence service can run locally or remotely. A remote model call still sends the selected context to that provider.

2. Obtain service access

Your operator creates a tenant and binds its access before issuing a scoped key, or binds your identity-provider subject. There is no automatic account creation from an unverified email address or a token's tenant claim.

For Model Context Protocol clients, configure the endpoint shown in the workspace and supply its service token through your client's supported secret mechanism. Use the exact protocol version returned by the service. Do not put tokens in a URL, a shared Markdown file, or a checked-in client configuration.

3. Bring your own model keys

Keep model credentials on the machine or broker that performs the model call. Store only a secret reference in shared configuration. The browser workspace never asks for a model provider key.

credential_ref: env:YOUR_PROVIDER_KEY
allow_network: false

This is a configuration pattern, not an executable universal provider file. Use the selected adapter's documented schema. Enable network calls only after choosing the exact provider, model, task allowance, and disclosure scope.

A native harness may use its own supported sign-in. A brokered tool can instead use a host-held credential on behalf of a scoped assignment. Neither arrangement removes the provider's terms, account limits, or required permissions.

4. Verify the connection

Connect to the workspace and confirm the tenant, namespace and scopes. Search for a permitted item. Inspect its identity, qualification basis and digest. Fetching a file does not prove that your harness loaded it or used it correctly.

If access expires, reconnect with a valid token. If a download or checkout has an uncertain outcome, inspect its recorded state before repeating the operation. Do not assume a timed-out action was cancelled.

Privacy and telemetry

Do not include keys in prompts, intelligence bodies, screenshots, logs, or feedback. Embeddings and raw context are confidential data, not anonymous telemetry. Choose retention and improvement consent separately from execution access.

HOW IT WORKS

Big problems.
Clear steps.

Start with what you want to achieve. Break the work into steps, give each step relevant expertise and tools, then check the result before moving on.

The plan can change as you learn more. A step can ask for missing information, try another approach or send unfinished work back for improvement, within the limits you set.

SEE WHAT EACH STEP NEEDS

Prepare a customer import without changing the original.
Example only · no work runs here

Choose a step to see its information, tools and expected result. The person inspecting the data needs different material from the person checking the finished import.

01
Understand the input
02
Choose an approach
03
Build or reuse
04
Check the result

UNDERSTAND

Understand the inputs before changing anything.

Read a sample, identify the columns and flag missing or unclear values. Keep the original file unchanged.

How this step could run
A research session

A short brief, the selected sample and read-only tools.

Information for this step
Selected files
Step instructions
task.json

What to inspect, what to report and what must stay unchanged.

Expert guidance

Definitions for the columns in this file.

Task files

Relevant past mistakes, such as losing leading zeroes in customer numbers.

What it can do

Read the selected files and check their contents. This step cannot change the input or browse unrelated files.

What it cannot access
The rest of the customer archive
Permission to change the original file
Billing and model-provider keys
What you get

A report of the columns, unclear values and questions that affect the import.

When this step is finished

This is an illustration, not a recorded customer result. Selecting a step does not access your files or call a model.

USEFUL INFORMATION, WHEN IT IS NEEDED

Give each step a useful starting point.
Find
Look for relevant guidance and reusable code
Choose
Check that it fits the task and your permissions
Prepare
Give the step its selected files and instructions
Work
Use an appropriate model, tool or existing code
Check
Test the result against your requirements

A useful briefing is not always the shortest one. Start with relevant information and add more when the work reveals a gap.

What if a step needs more information?

USE WHAT SUITS THE WORK

Not every step needs a large model.

The goal and quality checks stay the same. The way a step does the work can vary.

Build something new
A focused AI workspace

Give your chosen development tool a clear brief, selected files and the permissions needed to build or repair the missing pieces.

Make a choice
A smaller, focused request

A decision may need one model request rather than a complete development session. Use a compatible model service you have already configured.

Reuse existing work
Run code that already fits

Use reviewed code when it meets the requirements. That step may need no model call and no newly generated code.

Models may run on your machine or through a provider you choose. You supply access; Baltor does not need to install or host the models for you.

MAKE THE EFFORT COUNT

Is your AI spending effort in the wrong places?

These are the questions Baltor is designed to address at each step of the work.

INFORMATION
Too much context for a small task?

Match information to the task. Bring in more when it helps, without making every step carry the whole history.

Relevant information, less repetition
MODEL SELECTION
An expensive model for every decision?

Compare suitable models and reusable code for each step, against your quality and spending requirements.

An approach that fits the work
DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE
Missing the right domain expertise?

Bring relevant methods, examples and checks into the work, with sources and applicability kept visible.

Specific guidance, not generic guesses
CODE REUSE
Paying to rewrite code that already exists?

Find an eligible implementation first. Generate new code for the gaps instead of reproducing a known solution as more output tokens.

Reuse what is already qualified
IMPROVEMENT
Are the same mistakes showing up again?

Keep useful results and corrections. Compare proposed improvements on real tasks before making them the default.

Measured improvement, not blind repetition

BUILDING BLOCKS FOR BETTER SOLUTIONS

Put knowledge, code and experience to work.

Useful intelligence includes how to approach the work, code that can do it, what happened before, and what you want done differently.

01 / Approach
Context Intelligence

Methods, questions, constraints, examples and output contracts that guide the work.

For the import task

A field-definition guide and a checklist for missing values.

02 / Reuse
Code Intelligence

Reusable functions, tools, packages and workflows with declared inputs, outputs and effects.

For the import task

A qualified normalizer with its dependency and verification records.

03 / Experience
Runtime History and Solution Intelligence

Saved outcomes, failures, repairs, measurements and solution information that can inform a new task.

For the import task

A previous import's failed assumptions and the checks that detected them.

04 / Guidance
User Feedback Intelligence

Scoped corrections, priorities and instructions supplied by a person.

For the import task

“Keep uncertain matches for review. Never overwrite the original file.”

The four layers describe the broader product. The hosted service currently provides a small Context Intelligence example; it does not yet offer a populated catalogue across every layer.

YOUR TOOLS, WITH HELP FROM BALTOR

Get useful material. Keep control of your work.
BALTOR
A library of useful material

Check that each download matches the version you chose

Matching results or the permitted download

Through your signed-in connection

YOUR ENVIRONMENT
Your task and tools
Set the goal and limits
Decide what success means and what the work may access
Carry out each step
Use your chosen models, development tools or existing code
Keep the results
Inspect files, checks and the record of what happened

Your tools work within the permissions you set.

MODEL ACCESS IS SEPARATE
Your tools connect to your chosen model

Model keys stay in your environment or its approved credential manager. A remote model may receive the information you allow your tools to send.

The website does not automatically upload your complete task files or conversations. The full workflow shown here is a product design; the service currently supports search and selected-file delivery.
Available today

A person with an account can sign in with a service token, search the small example library, download permitted files and view usage. Administrators can create and revoke test tokens.

The complete example above is still being tested from start to finish. Public account creation, paid subscriptions and automatic setup of every step are not open yet. We have not established token savings or overnight task completion for this release.
